territorial_scope.description: Applies to financial regulatory agencies and regulated entities of the United States as defined in Sec. 2(7) and Sec. 2(8).

evidence.quote: The term “regulated entity” means an entity regulated by any financial regulatory agency.

summary.short: Creates AI Innovation Labs at US financial regulatory agencies. Regulated entities may apply to run AI test projects under alternative compliance strategies approved by the agency, with enforcement limited to the approved terms. Agencies must issue implementing rules within 180 days of enactment.
summary.long: S.2528 (Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act) would require each financial regulatory agency to establish, or designate, an AI Innovation Lab where regulated entities may run AI test projects under alternative compliance strategies that waive or modify specified agency regulations. Applications must describe the project, the regulation to be waived or modified, an assessment of public interest, systemic risk, anti-money laundering consistency and national security risk, a termination date, limits on size and growth, a business plan and an economic impact estimate. Agencies must decide within 120 days, extendable once by 120 days; an application still undecided after the extension is deemed approved. During an approved project, the agency may enforce the waived regulation only as set out in the strategy, but fraud and unsafe or unsound practices remain enforceable. Denied applicants may resubmit no more than two substantially similar applications, and agencies may sue to enjoin projects that present an immediate danger or specified risks. Agencies must issue regulations within 180 days of enactment after a 60-day comment period, and must submit annual reports on project outcomes beginning two years after enactment and continuing for seven years thereafter.

notes: Bill text as introduced (S.2528); the document carries no version date. The bill amends, repeals and implements no existing statute and states no enabling act. All listed relations are cross-references: Sec. 2 incorporates other Acts by definition, and Sec. 3 uses AML obligations as an application criterion. Target IDs are not verified against the registry. Internal tension: Sec. 3(a)(2)(B)(i) requires a written agency determination within 120 days, but Sec. 3(a)(2)(B)(iv) deems an application approved if no determination is made after a 120-day extension. The text contains no general effective-date provision; Sec. 3(a)(2)(D) requires regulations within 180 days of enactment.
